args.sql: SELECT MIN(event_time), MAX(event_time), MIN(signup_date), MAX(signup_date), COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT usr_id) FROM users_data

SELECT substr(signup_date,1,7) m, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) users, SUM(event_time < signup_date) ev_before_signup, COUNT(DISTINCT signup_date||'-'||user_id) - COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) multi_signup FROM users_data GROUP BY m ORDER BY m

toolCalls.name: db__run_query

args.sql:
WITH u AS (
  SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd,
    MAX(julianday(substr(event_time,1,10)) - julianday(signup_date)) max_day
  FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT COALESCE(substr(sd,1,7),'Q3 2026 total') AS cohort, COUNT(*) AS users,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(max_day>=1)/COUNT(*),1) AS d1_pct,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(max_day>=7)/COUNT(*),1) AS d7_pct,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(max_day>=14)/COUNT(*),1) AS d14_pct,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(max_day>=30)/COUNT(*),1) AS d30_pct
FROM u WHERE sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY substr(sd,1,7) WITH ROLLUP

finalText:
I calculated retention for users who signed up last quarter, put the results in a new spreadsheet and posted a summary with the link to #analytics.

The data runs through 2026-11-11, so I took "last quarter" to mean the last full one: Q3 2026 (July–September), 354 users. I counted a user as kept at Day N if they did anything in the product N or more days after signing up.

| Signup month | Users | Day 7 | Day 14 | Day 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2026 | 121 | 92.6% | 80.2% | 62.8% |
| Aug 2026 | 118 | 84.7% | 76.3% | 67.8% |
| Sep 2026 | 115 | 85.2% | 73.0% | 62.6% |
| **Q3 total** | **354** | **87.6%** | **76.6%** | **64.4%** |

- **Day-1 retention shows as 100% in every month.** That's because every Q3 user was active at least once after their signup day. So it doesn't tell you much. If you want a stricter "came back the next day" number, I can calculate retention for exact days or weeks instead.
- **There's no Day-60 figure.** Users who signed up in late September haven't been around for 60 days yet, so the data can't show it for all of Q3.
- **Column name mismatch:** the table's description lists the user column as `usr_id`, but it's actually called `user_id`. Someone may want to fix the description.

Spreadsheet: https://sheets.example.com/sh1
